Tesla FSD V14 handles a human hand signal flawlessly.

In a new clip shared by reddituser4049, the vehicle recognizes a hand gesture, stops and waits appropriately before continuing.

These small interactions matter more than raw highway driving. Real-world human behavior is unpredictable, and smooth communication between people and autonomous systems is one of the hardest parts of self-driving.

Moments like this show how much more natural FSD behavior is becoming.

My dad is a disabled Vietnam veteran. My wife and I are his caregivers now—we handle pretty much everything.

But driving? Not anymore thanks to our Tesla Cybertruck.

Twice a week, his VA day-activity program gives him amazing time with folks his age — games, stories, independence. And every trip (20 min each way), my truck TARS handles it all.

Sure, I’m in the driver’s seat, but really just along to visit with him: coffee, conversation, music. 

The truck does all of the work. 

It manages the backroads, highway, merging, traffic, school zones, parking… everything.

I get quality time with my dad.

He loves it. 

And every time we pull up, he says the same thing:

“Good job, truck.” ❤️📐

We hop out and I easily unload his heavy specialized walker — it fits perfectly in the rear bed under the tonneau cover.

Grateful for this technology that helps our heroes and their families. 

What has your Tesla done for the elderly, veterans, or caregiving in your life? @Tesla @elonmusk @DeptVetAffairs

Neuralink’s robotic surgical system uses a custom-designed needle to grasp and insert each ultra-flexible electrode thread directly into brain tissue.

These needles are fully engineered and manufactured in house at Neuralink.

Using precision lasers, we mill microscopic features smaller than what the naked eye can see to enable secure grip and ultra gentle insertion with minimal trauma.

This advanced microfabrication and vertical integration improves implantation accuracy, reliability, and safety key steps toward scalable, high-performance brain-computer interfaces.

Starship Flight 12 is getting close.

Ship 39, the massive upper stage for Starship V3, is now moving through Starbase as SpaceX enters final launch preparations.

The current target date is May 15, 2026, marking what could become the first flight of the V3 generation. Expectations are high as SpaceX pushes for bigger upgrades in performance, reliability and reusability.

Momentum around Starship is accelerating fast.
